To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
students' learning styles are relatively stable, but their approaches to studying vary across different learning situations.
students' approaches to learning are determined by their conceptions of the learning situation and their conceptions about learning.
students' learning styles are stable and are determined by their conceptions of the purpose of learning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how students learn in higher education and the implications for teaching.
how students' conceptions and perceptions of their contexts influence their approaches to studying.
the development of students' learning strategies, their conceptions of the learning process and their conceptions about the nature of knowledge and how it is best learnt.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
students' learning styles are contextually driven, that their learning styles and conceptions of learning are interrelated and that both are stable.
learning style research has a great deal to contribute to the understanding of students' conceptions and approaches to learning.
students' approaches to learning and learning styles are both contextually and personally determined.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the learning style concept has to be redefined.
students' learning styles are not stable, but that their conceptions of the learning process are.
learning styles are stable and contextually driven, and that they are related to conceptions of learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
students' approaches to learning and learning styles should not be seen as competing concepts.
students' conceptions and approaches to studying are interrelated and that these relationships should be taken into account when designing teaching and learning interventions.
the two approaches are complementary, rather than contradictory.
